# Intuition :

Economic development linked to a reduction of gender inequities ?

# Data we used

 - Economic productivity : GDP / hours worked  (using PPP)
 - Gender inequities : Gender wage gap (% of male median wages)

:::{.notes}
 - Economic productivity : GDP per hours worked (using purchasing power parity)
 - Gender inequities : Gender wage gap (difference between median wages, as a percentage of male median wages)
:::

:::{.notes}
About the data : tiers are 3-quantiles (each tier has the same amount of country)

 - variance comes from the lower-third :
     - contains both the high-gap south KORea
     - AND near-perfect parity countries like BulGaRia

 - still outlying : LUXembourg
     - the only one with negative gender gap (i.e. whomen are paid more than men on median)
     - we can see that it's outlying because it's beyond the "minimum box"
:::
